history.pageHint: Every change to a configuration resource: who made it, when, from where (web, CLI, apply, Terraform, a task) and why. Open a row to compare it and restore it.
history.emptyHint: History starts when the cluster finished its upgrade to this version. Widen the period or clear the filters.
history.emptyResource: No recorded changes to this resource.
history.onlySet: Showing changes made by apply set {{name}}.
history.resourceHint: Changes to this resource, newest first. Open one to compare it or restore it.
history.secretHint: Secrets are not kept in the history: only whether they were set or changed. Restoring keeps the current secret.

restore.title: Restore {{name}} to revision {{revision}}?
restore.hint: The server plans the change; nothing is written until you restore. Secrets, the name and the power state are not restored. Every field goes back to that revision — fields it left at their defaults are reset; secrets added since stay.
restore.recreateHint: The resource comes back with the same id, so what pointed at it works again. Its data (disks, backups) is not restored.
restore.nothing: The resource already matches this revision.
restore.nameTaken: The name {{name}} is used by another resource now. Give a new name to recreate it under (it gets a new id).
restore.changed: The plan changed while you were reading it. Review it again and restore.
restore.stale: The resource changed or the plan expired. Review the new plan and restore again.
restore.force: Take over from Terraform and restore anyway
restore.forceHint: Terraform manages this resource. Restoring it here makes it differ from your Terraform configuration, so the next terraform apply changes it back unless you update the configuration too.

point.open: Restore to a point in time…
point.title: Restore to a point in time
point.hint: Put every resource in the scope back the way it was at that time. Review the server's plan before restoring. Every field goes back to that revision — fields it left at their defaults are reset; secrets added since stay.
point.scopeNeeded: Choose a folder, an apply set or a kind.
point.dataLoss: Also delete VMs, volumes and backup stores created since then (their data is lost)
